The examinations revealed a residual S. mansoni infection with the following parasite loads: 60, 192 and 156 eggs per gram of feces respectively.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old female from S. mansoni-endemic municipalities (Cabo de Santo Agostinho and Jaboatão dos Guararapes) with history of river bathing presented with strong left iliac pain beginning mid-2014. Initial workup (September-October 2014) revealed enlarged left ovary with cyst (2.84 cm, volume 16.82 cm3) on ultrasonography and MRI concerning for neoplasia, but tumor markers were normal. Left ovariectomy was performed in April 2015. Histopathological examination identified granulomatous inflammatory processes surrounding viable and calcified S. mansoni eggs without neoplastic tissue, establishing the diagnosis of ovarian schistosomiasis. Subsequent parasitological workup (April 2016) using Kato-Katz method confirmed residual S. mansoni infection (60-192 eggs per gram). The patient received three courses of praziquantel 50 mg/kg at two-month intervals due to the ectopic disease form and was followed as an outpatient.
